mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots-for is above the competition mean AND Team B's fouls-against is above the competition mean simultaneously. Measure Team A's corner-kicks-for in those jointly-conditioned matches versus the baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner-kick production rises when both Team A's shot volume is elevated and Team B's foul rate is elevated, more than either condition alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its conversion to shots-on-target is relatively modest, while Team B concedes a high volume of fouls (suggesting defensive pressure). The joint relationship between Team A's shots-for and Team B's fouls-against — two distinct observables from opposite sides — may predict corner-kick generation beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team A shots-for AND Team B fouls-against), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession-holding team (Team A role) holds possession above a threshold AND the defending team (Team B role) commits fouls above a threshold. Measure cards_2h for the defending team in those jointly-conditioned matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The defending team's second-half card accumulation rises as the joint combination of opponent possession dominance and own foul rate increases, beyond what either variable alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A dominates possession (all-prior ~58%, recent ~58%) while Team B commits fouls at a high rate (all-prior ~13.5, against ~15.8 — well above competition mean ~12.9). The joint relationship between Team A's possession advantage and Team B's foul rate may produce an asymmetric card-loading pattern in the second half, where Team B accumulates cards-2h at a rate above what either team's individual card profile predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: one team's possession level combined with the opposing team's foul rate predicting the opposing team's card outcome — two distinct observables from different sides, not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals by half for both teams simultaneously. Measure the interaction between Team A's 2H-vs-1H goal-for ratio and Team B's 1H-vs-2H goals-against ratio to identify whether the half in which goals are most likely to occur is jointly determined by both teams' half-level profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's second-half goal-scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's first-half goals-conceded rate exceeds its second-half rate, the match's goal distribution across halves is more skewed toward the second half than competition baseline, but the asymmetry between the two teams' half profiles creates a non-additive joint pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores goals at a markedly higher rate in the second half than the first half (1H: ~0.755, 2H: ~1.108), while Team B concedes goals at a markedly higher rate in the first half than the second half (1H: ~0.676, 2H: ~0.490). This asymmetric half-level goal-scoring profile across the two teams — Team A back-loaded, Team B front-loaded in conceding — creates a joint within-match state structure that is not captured by full-match goal averages alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct half-level splits from two different teams (Team A's 2H goal-for vs 1H goal-for AND Team B's 1H goals-against vs 2H goals-against), which is a within-match state interaction across two observables from different sides — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team's shots-on-target-to-shots ratio is above a threshold AND the defending team's fouls-against rate is above a threshold. Measure the attacking team's goals-for in those jointly-conditioned matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-for rises more steeply when both shot quality (SOT/shots ratio) is high AND the opponent's foul rate is high, compared to when only one condition holds — suggesting a super-additive or threshold interaction between the two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) is relatively high (SOT ~5.4 vs shots ~13.75, all-prior), while Team B's shots-on-target rate is lower (SOT ~4.27 vs shots ~11.62). Meanwhile, Team B concedes fouls at a high rate (~15.8 against, well above competition ~12.9). The joint relationship between Team A's shot quality (shots-on-target as a share of shots) and Team B's defensive foul rate may predict Team A's goal output beyond what either observable alone captures — specifically, whether high shot quality combined with a high-fouling opponent produces a non-linear uplift in goals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shot quality ratio and opponent foul rate) from different sides, requiring simultaneous conditioning on both — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Identify matches where a team's recent-5 yellow-card rate is substantially below its all-prior rate (suppressed regime) AND the opponent's fouls-against rate is above the competition mean. Measure cards_2h for both teams in those jointly-conditioned matches versus the baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team is in a suppressed recent yellow-card regime but faces an opponent that draws fouls at an elevated rate, second-half card accumulation reverts toward or exceeds the longer-run mean rather than continuing the suppressed trend — a regime-reversion pattern conditioned on the opponent's foul-drawing profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards have dropped sharply in recent matches (recent-5: ~0.6 vs all-prior: ~1.98), while Team B's fouls-against (fouls conceded by opponents of Team B) are high (~15.8 all-prior). The divergence between Team A's recent disciplinary trend and its longer-run profile, combined with Team B's persistent high-foul-drawing tendency, creates a cross-observable regime structure: when a team's recent card rate is in a suppressed regime relative to its own history AND the opponent draws fouls at an elevated rate, the second-half card accumulation pattern may differ from what either team's standalone card profile predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a sequencing/regime structure (recent vs all-prior card rate divergence) combined with a cross-team observable (opponent foul-drawing rate), jointly conditioning on two distinct dimensions from different observables and different teams — not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison alone.
